title: Security posture discovery with Praxis Health
next_steps: Maya to share SOC2 Type II report and ISO27001 scoping doc
Carlos to schedule a private deployment architecture deep dive (VPC/on-prem) next week
Ethan to send benchmark spreadsheet and sample latency/cost numbers for their workload
Redwood to provide SSO/SAML integration guide and example SAML metadata file
Praxis to confirm procurement timeline and security questionnaire owners
action_items: Maya Patel: send SOC2 Type II, penetration test summary, and security pack (due: 2026-03-24)
Carlos Reyes: schedule VPC/private deployment follow-up and draft network diagram (due: 2026-03-29)
Ethan Liu: share benchmark sheet and suggested instance/quantization profile (due: 2026-03-25)
Aisha Khan: provide sample data retention policy and list of regulated datasets (due: 2026-04-01)
summary: Praxis Health ran through Redwood's security posture and how hosted/dedicated/private deployments map to their requirements. Primary concerns: SOC2/ISO proof, SSO/SAML for IdP, RBAC and least-privilege, audit logs and retention, encryption/KMS (BYOK/HSM), and data residency/retention policies. Redwood agreed to send SOC2 artifacts, SSO integration docs, and a private deployment deep dive. Next step: architecture deep dive and benchmarks.
topics: Audit logs, retention and log streaming
Encryption at rest/in transit, KMS / BYOK / HSM
Network connectivity: VPC peering and on-prem options
Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private tradeoffs and timelines
transcript:
[00:00] Maya Patel: Hey everyone, thanks for hopping on, I'm Maya from Redwood, AE for this region. Carlos (SE) and Ethan (solutions) are here as well.
[00:06] Rajiv Sharma: Hi Maya, thanks. We just wanted to focus on security posture — we've got a pretty strict compliance bar.
[00:12] Linda Gomez: Yeah our security team needs to validate SOC2 and ISO evidence, SSO integration, and how logs are retained.
[00:20] Carlos Reyes: Great, we'll walk through how Redwood maps to those controls, and then dig into specifics for private deployment for PH.
[00:28] Aisha Khan: Quick note — we're evaluating hosted API first but core PH workloads will probably need dedicated or private because of PHI and residency.
[00:36] Maya Patel: Totally understood. Quick housekeeping: we'll capture action items, send SOC2 artifacts, and follow up on a technical deep dive for private.
[00:45] Rajiv: timeline wise, procurement wants answers by mid-April, ideally a pilot in May.
[00:51] Carlos: That seems doable, we'll align on docs. So first, SOC2 and ISO — Redwood has SOC2 Type II for the hosted control plane and Dedicated/Private have similar controls, we can share the report.
[01:03] Tom Becker: Can you confirm whether the SOC2 report covers data at rest encryption and key management?
[01:07] Maya: Yes, the report covers encryption at rest, and we have a KMS integration. For private we support BYOK and HSM-backed KMS options.
[01:15] Linda: BYOK meaning we can bring our own keys and control them? We need key separation and customer-managed keys.
[01:20] Carlos: Correct, BYOK for Private and Dedicated via customer-managed KMS — you can rotate keys, audit access, and we surface key-use logs to your audit stream.
[01:29] Aisha: And for hosted — do you offer KMS with customer keys?
[01:33] Maya: For hosted, we offer an encrypted-at-rest model with Redwood-managed KMS; for customers requiring BYOK we recommend Dedicated or Private.
[01:39] Rajiv: Ok. Next SSO: we need SAML 2.0 and SCIM provisioning for RBAC. Who owns the IdP integration?
[01:46] Ethan Liu: Redwood supports SAML SSO and SCIM for user provisioning, plus role-based access controls. We can provide example metadata and step-by-step guides.
[01:54] Linda: Do roles map to our LDAP groups? We need least privilege, runbook for access revocation.
[01:59] Carlos: You can sync groups via SCIM. RBAC is flexible — we have role templates and can map to custom groups. We'll share the SAML metadata and SCIM schema.
[02:08] Rajiv: Audit logging — we need an immutable audit trail with 1 year retention, and ability to stream logs to our SIEM.
[02:14] Maya: We can export audit logs to your CloudWatch/Stackdriver/Splunk — log streaming is supported and retention is configurable. For Private you control retention fully.
[02:23] Tom: Is there support for write once read many logs or WORM?
[02:27] Carlos: We don't provide a WORM store natively, but you can route logs to a WORM-compliant service on your side; we'll deliver signed, time-stamped audit events.
[02:36] Aisha: About network — we have a corporate requirement for no public egress for certain datasets. How would Private look?
[02:41] Ethan: Private deployment can be VPC-isolated, either customer-hosted or in your cloud tenant. You can control egress and enforce private connectivity via VPC peering or Transit Gateway.
[02:52] Rajiv: For Dedicated, are there tenancy guarantees?
[02:55] Maya: Dedicated gives you reserved GPU pools and network isolation within our infra; for strict no-public-egress we recommend Private in your VPC or on-prem.
[03:03] Linda: Encryption in transit — TLS mutual auth?
[03:06] Carlos: All traffic is TLS 1.2/1.3. For Private we can add mTLS between components if required.
[03:12] Rajiv: How do you handle model weights — are they stored encrypted?
[03:16] Maya: Model artifacts and KV cache are encrypted at rest; keys are KMS-managed. For Private we can keep keys in your KMS.
[03:22] Aisha: Any caveats around caching — like KV cache containing customer prompts?
[03:26] Carlos: We do prefix and KV caching to improve latency; for regulated data we recommend disabling cache or using an isolated cache per tenant, and for Private you control cache placement.
[03:36] Linda: Data retention policies — we need to ensure user prompt logs are only retained 30 days unless explicitly retained. Can you configure that?
[03:42] Maya: Yes, retention windows are configurable per-route; we can set default 30 days and have policy for longer retention if you opt-in. We'll share the retention config doc.
[03:51] Rajiv: Are there background processes that access logs — like support staff troubleshooting? We need RBAC and audit around that.
[03:57] Carlos: Access for support is role-based and requires requester approval; all access is logged in the audit trail.
[04:04] Tom: Pen tests and vuln scanning — do you run regular pentests and provide summaries?
[04:08] Maya: Yes, we run annual penetration tests and quarterly internal scanning; we'll provide a summary and remediation timelines.
[04:15] Aisha: What about supply chain and model provenance — can you attest to model sources?
[04:20] Ethan: We maintain a model catalog with provenance and vetted performance profiles; we can provide a bill of materials for the models you plan to use.
[04:29] Rajiv: A few specific asks from procurement: 1) SOC2 Type II report, 2) encryption and BYOK details, 3) SSO integration doc, 4) network diagram for private deployment. Can you align on delivery?
[04:41] Maya: We'll deliver those — SOC2 and pen test summary by Wednesday, SSO/SCIM docs and a sample SAML metadata file by Friday, and Carlos will draft a VPC/network diagram for the private deep dive.
[04:53] Linda: On the hosted vs dedicated tradeoff, cost is a factor but security is primary; if Private is required it will be a longer procurement path.
[04:58] Carlos: Understood. We typically start with hosted for non-PHI workloads, then move to Dedicated or Private for PHI. We can also run a dedicated pilot to validate perf and controls.
[05:08] Rajiv: About monitoring and incidents — do you provide SOC/incident alert integrations and playbooks?
[05:13] Maya: Yes, we have incident response playbooks and can integrate with pager/sentry/opsgenie; we'll share the playbook summary.
[05:21] Tom: Any certifications in flight? ISO27001?
[05:24] Maya: We're currently in scoping for ISO27001 and can share our control mapping.
[05:29] Linda: Regulatory question — do you support data residency in EU regions? For us we need certain workloads in-country.
[05:35] Ethan: We support region pinning for models and storage, especially in Dedicated/Private. For hosted we have region options but contracts can specify residency requirements.
[05:44] Aisha: A quick thing — our engineers will want sample keys and code for SAML and API calls.
[05:48] Carlos: We'll include example SAML metadata and a tiny quickstart repo link in the follow-up.
[05:55] Rajiv: Anything about vendor lock-in — we need exit procedures and data export options.
[05:59] Maya: We provide data export and can scrub or export logs and models on contract termination; we'll document the offboarding steps.
[06:08] Tom: Ok that's helpful. On SLAs — what uptime and latency SLAs exist for Dedicated?
[06:12] Carlos: Dedicated has SLA-backed uptime and latency targets; we'll share the SLA doc and typical latency percentiles for similar workloads.
[06:20] Linda: One last item — the security questionnaire we have is long, can you assign a contact to work through it?
[06:25] Maya: I'll own the questionnaire with Tom and Carlos helping on technical Qs.
[06:29] Rajiv: Great thanks.
[06:32] Maya: To recap action items: we'll send SOC2 and pen test summary, SSO/SCIM docs, benchmark sheet, and schedule the private architecture deep dive. Anything else?
[06:41] Aisha: No that's it. We'll review artifacts and get procurement timeline.
[06:45] Tom: Thanks folks.
[06:47] Maya: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the docs and invite for the architecture session.
[06:51] [call ends]
